# secobserve_user (Resource)

A local SecObserve user, manageable by a superuser through the API.

~> Users created this way have **no usable password**: the write endpoint this resource uses has no password field. Set one out of band with `PATCH /api/users/{id}/change_password/`, which requires the caller's own current password and so cannot be done by this provider, or have the user authenticate via OIDC instead.

On an OIDC-enabled instance, prefer the `secobserve_user` data source to *reference* users provisioned just-in-time at login, rather than this resource: SecObserve overwrites `email`, `full_name`, `first_name` and `last_name` from the identity token on every OIDC login, fighting anything Terraform sets here. `is_active`, `is_superuser` and `is_external` are not touched by login and remain safely Terraform-managed even for an OIDC user.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Local user, not OIDC-provisioned. Has no usable password until one is set
# out of band -- see the resource documentation.
resource "secobserve_user" "ci_bot" {
  username     = "ci-bot"
  first_name   = "CI"
  last_name    = "Bot"
  email        = "ci-bot@example.com"
  is_active    = true
  is_superuser = false
  is_external  = false
}

# Referencing an existing user -- OIDC-provisioned or not -- without
# Terraform claiming ownership of it.
data "secobserve_user" "alice" {
  username = "alice"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `username` (String) Username. Globally unique.

### Optional

- `email` (String) Email address.
- `first_name` (String) First name.
- `full_name` (String) Display name.

~> SecObserve recomputes this from `first_name` and `last_name` on every write whenever either is non-empty, overriding whatever is set here. It is only honored as given when both are empty. Leave it unset unless you are deliberately setting a display name for a user with no first or last name.
- `is_active` (Boolean) Whether the user can authenticate.
- `is_external` (Boolean) Whether the user is external. External users cannot create products or product groups.
- `is_superuser` (Boolean) Whether the user has superuser privileges: full read/write access regardless of product membership, and the ability to manage other users, general rules, instance settings and periodic tasks.
- `last_name` (String) Last name.

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) Numeric id of the user.
- `is_oidc_user` (Boolean) Whether SecObserve considers this an OIDC-provisioned user. Read-only: set by SecObserve itself on first OIDC login, never by this resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The exact username also works as the id.
import {
  to = secobserve_user.ci_bot
  id = "7"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Either the numeric id or the exact username works.
terraform import secobserve_user.ci_bot 7
terraform import secobserve_user.ci_bot "ci-bot"
```
